question: The agricultural sector in the EU is facing a significant demographic challenge. The average age of farmers in the EU is 57 years old, while only about 12 % of farmers are under the age of 40, highlighting a clear trend of an ageing farming population.

At the same time, older farmers are often less likely to adopt digital tools, which can make it more difficult for them to access agricultural support schemes, submit applications and participate in EU-funded projects. This creates an additional barrier to ensuring equal access to financial support and modernisation opportunities across the sector.
In the light of these challenges, could the Commission answer the following: 1.

What specific EU financial programmes and instruments are currently available to support the digital education and upskilling of farmers, particularly older farmers, with the aim of facilitating their access to agricultural subsidies, funding schemes and project applications?
Does the Commission plan to introduce additional targeted measures within the common agricultural policy or other EU funding frameworks to improve digital accessibility for farmers?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (18.6.2026) 1. The Commission acknowledges the importance of digital education, advisory support and upskilling to ensure broad and inclusive access to digital technologies across the farming population.

The Common Agricultural Policy1 supports this objective through interventions linked to Agricultural Knowledge and Innovation Systems (AKIS), including advisory services, knowledge exchange (for example, training and advice), and EIP-AGRI Operational Groups2.

Horizon Europe also promotes digital skills in agriculture by involving farmers in the design of solutions tailored to their needs, notably through the multi-actor approach3. Thematic networks4 and advisory networks5 further support digital education and access to innovative digital tools by collecting and disseminating knowledge among practitioners.

Several Horizon Europe projects provide farmers with learning material and recommendations on the selection and use of digital tools. Additional support is available through cohesion-policy funds - notably ESF+6 for skills - and national recovery and resilience plans7. 2.

The Commission’s proposals for the 2028–2034 multiannual financial framework prioritise digital transformation, with the EU farming sector set to benefit through several instruments, including the national and regional partnership plans8 (NRPPs), the European Competitiveness Fund9 and Horizon Europe10.
The NRPPs aligns with the Digital Decade11 objectives including digital skills - while leveraging tools and cross-policy synergies to drive a data-driven transition in agriculture.

1 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2021/2115/oj/eng. 2 EIP-AGRI: European Innovation Partnership for agricultural productivity and sustainability. 3 https://eu-cap-network.ec.europa.eu/multi-actor-projects-research-and-practice-co-creating-solutions_en. 4 https://eu-cap-network.ec.europa.eu/thematic-networks-compiling-knowledge-and-solutions-ready-practice_en. 5 https://eu-cap-network.ec.europa.
